meta.redaction_policy: Exploitable security specifics are redacted on the public site until remediation lands. Scores, verdicts, gate progress, and finding categories remain public. When a finding closes, flip status to fixed and the card unseals.

findings.title: Compliance engine is schema-only
findings.summary: The reactivation + Twilio compliance engine exists only as database tables. No send path, opt-out endpoint, DNC check, or Twilio client is wired.
findings.impact: Until enforcement ships, any outbound SMS or campaign email risks TCPA / A2P 10DLC / CAN-SPAM exposure with per-message statutory penalties. The only thing preventing a violation today is that sending is switched off.

findings.title: Production secrets in a dev-flagged environment
findings.summary: Live Twilio and FieldRoutes credentials sit in an environment configured for local development with debug mode on.
findings.impact: Debug mode can render detailed error output to visitors, and the credential set grants full CRM and SMS control. Secrets must be rotated and moved out of the web-facing configuration.

findings.title: Sign-in codes logged to plaintext disk
findings.summary: One-time login codes are written to a plaintext log file on every send, in every environment, not just development.
findings.impact: Anyone with filesystem read access can harvest live login codes for staff and customers, including admins, fully defeating the passwordless model. Logging must be gated to local dev and existing logs purged.

findings.title: No rate limit on code issue
findings.summary: The login-request step issues and emails a code with no rate-limit check; only the verify step is limited.
findings.impact: An attacker can flood a victim inbox with codes and burn send quota and cost, unbounded. The limiter must wrap the issue step, keyed per identity and per IP.

findings.title: Session cookie Secure flag unreliable behind proxy
findings.summary: The session cookie Secure flag is derived from signals a TLS-terminating proxy does not populate, and the forwarded-proto header is never read.
findings.impact: Session cookies can be issued without the Secure flag in production and sent over a plaintext hop. HTTPS redirect and HSTS are also still disabled.

findings.title: Regex-based rich-text sanitizer
findings.summary: CMS blog bodies are sanitized with regex and a tag allow-list that still permits anchors and images.
findings.impact: Regex HTML sanitization is reliably bypassable, leaving residual stored-XSS risk on every reader. Replace with a real allow-list sanitizer or a Markdown pipeline that escapes on render.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
findings.summary: Security headers are set, but a Content-Security-Policy header is absent.
findings.impact: Given a raw-HTML render path exists, a strict CSP is the cheapest defense-in-depth backstop against injected scripts.

findings.title: Role permissions defined but never enforced
findings.summary: The schema stores a JSON permissions array per role, but nothing reads it; authorization is role-string only.
findings.impact: Fine-grained access control is currently fictional. Any future staff-can-X-but-not-Y requirement has no enforcement hook. Wire a permission check or delete the column.

findings.title: Loose customer identifier matching
findings.summary: A customer is matched by email, phone, or account number, then the code is emailed to the address on file.
findings.impact: Loose identifier matching widens the surface for triggering codes against a known customer. Tighten matching and apply rate limiting keyed on the resolved identity.

findings.title: SQL identifiers interpolated in helpers
findings.summary: The database insert/update helpers bind all values but concatenate table and column names into the SQL string.
findings.impact: Safe only because every caller passes code-defined literals. The first developer to pass a user-controlled key opens a real injection. Allow-list identifiers against the schema.

findings.title: Contact form does not persist leads
findings.summary: The contact form validates and CSRF-checks correctly but only logs the submission and flashes a success message; nothing is stored.
findings.impact: Leads are silently dropped while the visitor is told the message was received. Functional defect with a mild trust cost.

findings.title: strip_tags used as a cleaning control
findings.summary: The validator clean() helper uses strip_tags on free-text fields.
findings.impact: A blunt instrument that gives false confidence. Output escaping is the real control; treat clean() as cosmetic.

findings.title: No commit history and no test suite
findings.summary: The repository has no tracked commits and no tests.
findings.impact: No regression test will catch a future removal of a CSRF check or a prepared-statement bypass. A durability problem for security controls.

findings.title: CSRF token is one-per-session
findings.summary: The CSRF token is issued once per session rather than per form.
findings.impact: Acceptable and standard. Rotation on login is handled via session regeneration. Noted for completeness.

findings.title: SSL verification disabled on FieldRoutes calls
findings.summary: Certificate verification is turned off on all FieldRoutes API calls, including the stream fallback.
findings.impact: API credentials travel over a connection that does not verify the server, exposing them to interception. Verification must be enabled before any production traffic.

findings.title: Dev server used as the production stack
findings.summary: The Dockerfile runs the PHP built-in single-threaded development server.
findings.impact: The built-in server handles one request at a time and is explicitly not intended for public networks. Replace with nginx + php-fpm.

findings.title: World-writable permissions in the image
findings.summary: The Dockerfile applies recursive 777 permissions to storage and database.
findings.impact: A security anti-pattern. Replace with a non-root user and targeted permissions.

findings.title: No .dockerignore
findings.summary: The full source tree, including the .env and the SQLite database, is copied into the image.
findings.impact: Secrets and runtime data ship inside the container. Add a .dockerignore to exclude .env, .git, database files, and logs.

findings.title: Zero git commits
findings.summary: The entire codebase is a single uncommitted working tree with no history.
findings.impact: No blame, no diff history, no rollback capability. An initial commit is step zero of production foundation.

findings.title: Role permissions never enforced by guards
findings.summary: Route guards check the role string only; the JSON permissions column is ignored.
findings.impact: A sales user can access everything a tech_support user can. Add a permission guard reading the JSON column.

findings.title: Sessions table defined but unused
findings.summary: A sessions table exists for server-side revocation, but the app uses PHP native file-based sessions.
findings.impact: Dead schema. Implement DB-backed sessions or remove the table.

findings.title: No test suite
findings.summary: There is no test directory and no test configuration anywhere.
findings.impact: The OTP, CSRF, rate limiter, and FieldRoutes upsert flows are testable in isolation but untested. Add PHPUnit/Pest with priority on those.

findings.title: No composer.json
findings.summary: There is no dependency manifest or autoloader config.
findings.impact: The hand-rolled autoloader works, but composer.json is the ecosystem standard and enables static analysis, testing, and linting tooling.

findings.title: Contact form does not persist leads
findings.summary: The contact submission handler is a TODO that only logs; it does not store, notify, or auto-reply.
findings.impact: Leads are dropped while the user is told the message was received.

findings.title: Fat controllers, empty Models and Services
findings.summary: All business logic lives in controllers; the Models/ and Services/ directories are empty.
findings.impact: StaffController mixes customer search, FieldRoutes sync, pagination, and a JSON API in one class. Works at 6,400 LOC but will not scale. Extract dedicated services.

findings.title: Controllers inherit from PageController
findings.summary: Auth, Admin, and Staff controllers extend the marketing PageController to reuse helpers.
findings.impact: Couples auth and admin logic to the marketing controller. A BaseController or trait is cleaner.

findings.title: Static classes block testability
findings.summary: Router, Database, Session, Csrf, Config, Logger, Geo, Validator, and RateLimiter are all static.
findings.impact: The Database singleton cannot be swapped for a test double. Introduce interfaces and dependency injection.

findings.title: No migration system
findings.summary: Schema version is hardcoded to 1 with idempotent CREATE TABLE only; there is no upgrade path.
findings.impact: When the schema evolves there is no ALTER-based migration path.

findings.title: No SQLite backup strategy
findings.summary: The database is a single file with no backup cron.
findings.impact: A disk failure or a bad migration destroys all data. Add a scheduled .backup to offsite storage.

findings.title: No static analysis
findings.summary: No PHPStan or Psalm configuration.
findings.impact: Given the strict_types discipline, adding PHPStan at level 6+ is low-effort, high-value.

findings.title: Twilio integration is schema-only
findings.summary: Environment variables and a live SID are configured, but no PHP code references Twilio.
findings.impact: Carrier-lookup and phone-risk tables are never written. Implement or remove the dead schema.

findings.title: Reactivation engine is schema-only
findings.summary: Campaign, send, and unsubscribe tables are fully designed but no controller or service implements them.
findings.impact: The retention engine cannot execute a single campaign. Implement or remove the dead schema.

findings.title: No CORS headers on the search API
findings.summary: The customer-search API route sets no CORS headers.
findings.impact: Add CORS middleware if the endpoint is consumed cross-origin.

findings.title: Identifiers built by concatenation
findings.summary: insert()/update() build table and column names by string concatenation.
findings.impact: Values are bound, but a whitelist check on identifiers is defensive insurance.

findings.title: Geo phone routing leaks Arizona visitors to Washington
findings.summary: The geo-aware phone helper is used in only 5 places while a hardcoded Washington number is the primary call CTA in 13 templates.
findings.impact: An Arizona visitor tapping the primary button on the prices, pest, services, about, areas, FAQs, referral, account, dashboard, or contact pages dials the Spokane line. A wrong-number conversion leak on the highest-intent action across roughly 80% of the marketing surface.

findings.title: Design system departs from the frozen baseline
findings.summary: The app ships an olive/khaki/orange tactical system while the frozen baseline specifies navy/green/amber with different type families.
findings.impact: Two live design systems is the real risk. Internal self-consistency is strong, but David and Washington must pick one identity and freeze it. A conformance pass is mostly a token remap.
findings.resolution_note: Awaiting David ruling: olive/orange tactical vs navy/amber baseline.

findings.title: No skip link and no global focus indicator
findings.summary: Focus styles exist only on form fields; links, nav, and buttons have no reliable visible focus state.
findings.impact: Keyboard users lose their place on a dark, animation-rich page. The frozen baseline specifies a 3px ring with 2px offset that is not implemented.

findings.title: Mobile call CTA hidden behind the hamburger
findings.summary: On small screens the phone button lives inside the collapsed nav drawer.
findings.impact: Pest control is a high-intent mobile-first vertical; a visitor with an active infestation should be one tap from the phone. Add a persistent mobile call bar.

findings.title: Pest library count mismatch
findings.summary: There are 26 live pests in the database, 27 image files, and 27 claimed in some copy.
findings.impact: One image (the pre-split flea/tick composite) is orphaned. Delete it and align all copy to the real count of 26.

findings.title: Nav CTA is phone-only
findings.summary: The navigation offers links plus a single phone CTA and no quote-form action.
findings.impact: Interior pages have no one-tap path to the quote form from the nav. Add a persistent Free Quote CTA.

findings.title: Contact form lacks field-level error semantics
findings.summary: The form does CSRF, validation, a summary, and value persistence right, but errors render only in a top summary.
findings.impact: No aria-invalid or aria-describedby links a field to its error, so screen-reader and mobile users must scroll to learn what failed.

findings.title: Pervasive inline styles
findings.summary: Nearly every page template carries inline style attributes that duplicate stylesheet utilities.
findings.impact: Makes a future token remap expensive and invites drift. Define utilities and strip the inline blocks alongside the palette ruling.

findings.title: Error pages drift from the palette
findings.summary: The 404 and 403 pages redefine their own root colors with a subtly different orange and load no fonts.
findings.impact: They fall back to system fonts, a visible brand drift on a page every lost visitor sees. Point them at shared tokens and load the fonts.

findings.title: Analytics disabled, paths unmeasured
findings.summary: The analytics IDs are blank and the enabled flag is off, so instrumentation exists but is dark.
findings.impact: Conversion performance cannot be scored and the routing leak cannot be seen in data until this is live.

findings.title: Hero HUD hardcodes Spokane coordinates
findings.summary: The home hero prints Spokane coordinates for every visitor regardless of region.
findings.impact: Cosmetic, but it undercuts the geo-localization the site otherwise does. Use a region-aware string or label it as HQ.

findings.title: Ticker city list duplicated in JS
findings.summary: The scrolling ticker hardcodes the 15-city list while the areas grid lists the same cities in markup.
findings.impact: Two sources of truth for service areas. Derive the ticker from the areas data.

findings.title: 99.7% of customers are cancelled
findings.summary: 693 of 695 customer rows are cancelled; the 2 active rows are seed fixtures, not real customers.
findings.impact: The reactivation engine has no viable audience and any active-customer query returns test data. David must clarify whether this is reality or a FieldRoutes sync/filter issue before templates are built against an empty list.
findings.resolution_note: Awaiting David ruling: reality vs sync/filter artifact.

findings.title: last_service is 100% null
findings.summary: The last_service column exists but the FieldRoutes sync never maps any source field to it.
findings.impact: Recency-based reactivation targeting (we have not seen you in 6 months) is impossible across all 695 customers. Populate from the lastCompleted field.

findings.title: Analytics is completely dark
findings.summary: No GA4 ID, analytics disabled, no conversion events, no pixel, no Clarity, no consent mode.
findings.impact: Every marketing dollar spent against this site is unattributable. The template is well-built and config-driven, so the fix is a one-line config change plus event wiring.

findings.title: Reactivation engine is hollow
findings.summary: Zero templates, zero campaigns, zero sends. The schema and unsubscribe architecture exist but no content has ever been loaded.
findings.impact: The retention engine is a skeleton with no muscle and cannot execute a single campaign.

findings.title: Seed data contaminates the customers table
findings.summary: Test fixtures live in the same customers table as FieldRoutes data with no source flag.
findings.impact: Any aggregate query (active count, average LTV, campaign audience) includes fake rows. Add a source column and tag the fixtures.

findings.title: Phone format inconsistency
findings.summary: 687 rows are 10-digit bare and 3 have a +1 prefix; there is no E.164 normalization.
findings.impact: Twilio SMS sends and carrier lookups will fail or misroute on non-normalized numbers. Normalize to E.164 on sync.

findings.title: Unsubscribe write-back not implemented
findings.summary: The design calls for syncing the no-call flag back to the FieldRoutes profile, but the API call does not exist.
findings.impact: If another system reads FieldRoutes directly it will not see the opt-out. A compliance gap.

findings.title: SSL verification disabled in the FieldRoutes client
findings.summary: Certificate verification is off in the FieldRoutes HTTP client.
findings.impact: API credentials in query parameters travel over an unverified connection. Interception exposure.

findings.title: Live credentials in a plaintext .env on disk
findings.summary: Live Twilio and FieldRoutes credentials are present in a plaintext .env file.
findings.impact: Git correctly excludes the file, but it exists on disk; any process with file read access has full CRM and SMS control.

findings.title: No sync scheduling
findings.summary: The FieldRoutes sync is a manual CLI script; the last run was 9 days stale at audit time.
findings.impact: Customer data drifts between runs; cancelled customers may receive reactivation messages. Schedule a sync every 6 hours.

findings.title: No incremental sync
findings.summary: Every run pulls all customers with no delta detection or updated-since filter.
findings.impact: Acceptable at current scale but will not survive 10K+ customers without API rate-limit issues.

findings.title: Duplicate emails and phones
findings.summary: 33 duplicate emails and 39 duplicate phones among customers, possibly legitimate family or shared accounts.
findings.impact: Campaign dedup logic must account for this; sending to all duplicate phone rows risks double-texting.

findings.title: content_blocks table is empty
findings.summary: The CMS block system is schema-ready but has zero content.
findings.impact: The admin CMS cannot edit page sections until blocks are populated.

findings.title: No per-run sync history
findings.summary: The last-sync summary is a single overwritten JSON blob.
findings.impact: Cannot answer what changed between syncs or audit sync behavior over time. Add a per-run history table.

findings.title: One malformed ZIP
findings.summary: One customer has a ZIP with the wrong length.
findings.impact: Minor. Does not affect routing or campaigns.

findings.title: Three arachnids mislabeled as insects
findings.summary: Scorpions, spiders, and ticks are categorized as insects; they are arachnids.
findings.impact: A basic biology error visible to any customer that damages credibility on a pest control site. Add an arachnid category and update the three pests.

findings.title: Moles labeled as rodents
findings.summary: Moles are categorized as rodents; they are insectivores.
findings.impact: Misleads treatment expectations: rodent bait does not work on moles, which require trapping or grub reduction. Recategorize as insectivore or wildlife.

findings.title: Multiple scientific names wrong or too narrow
findings.summary: Several pest pages list incorrect or overly narrow scientific names; flies and hornets are the most egregious.
findings.impact: Flies are listed as blow flies though the page covers fruit, drain, and house flies; hornets list a European species not established in the western US at all. An informed customer, inspector, or competitor could flag these. Correct to family-level or multi-genus language.

findings.title: No license numbers displayed
findings.summary: The site claims licensed, bonded, and insured but displays no license numbers.
findings.impact: WSDA requires the actual license number in advertising and AZ OPM requires it displayed in all advertising. A launch blocker for paid advertising. David must supply the WA and AZ structural pest control license numbers.
findings.resolution_note: Awaiting David: WA WSDA + AZ OPM license numbers.

findings.title: Unqualified pesticide safety claims
findings.summary: Family- and pet-safe claims lack label-direction and re-entry qualifications.
findings.impact: WSDA prohibits unqualified safe claims; no pesticide is universally safe. Qualify with applied-per-label and re-entry language and do not imply unconditional safety.

findings.title: Transparent-pricing claim with no prices shown
findings.summary: The pricing page says transparent online pricing but shows no prices.
findings.impact: A trust contradiction. The quote-based model is more compliant but loses the transparency differentiator. David must rule: publish real pricing or remove the claim.
findings.resolution_note: Awaiting David ruling: publish pricing or remove the claim.

findings.title: Arizona pest library gaps
findings.summary: The library is missing iconic Arizona pests.
findings.impact: Missing palo verde beetles (huge Phoenix search volume), kissing bugs (a Chagas vector), roof rats (the dominant Phoenix rat), earwigs, and stronger Africanized bee emphasis. Several pests also have regional mismatches for the AZ desert.

findings.title: No seasonal alert mechanism
findings.summary: The old site had a rotating seasonal alert banner; the new app has none.
findings.impact: No AZ monsoon scorpion/mosquito alerts, no WA rodent/termite/wasp alerts, no time-sensitive swarming or wasp-season messaging. A missed high-revenue, time-sensitive channel.

findings.title: Orphaned flea/tick image
findings.summary: fleas-ticks.jpg is orphaned after the flea/tick split; no database row references it.
findings.impact: The correct live pest count is 26, not 27. Delete or archive the orphan and update the seed comment.

findings.title: A few treatment claims overpromise
findings.summary: A handful of treatment phrases slightly overpromise.
findings.impact: Eliminated at the source and complete elimination are stronger than defensible; controlled and treatment-with-verification are safer. Tactical brand voice is fine for marketing but must not appear in regulatory filings.

findings.title: Marketing operability is 1/10 despite 8/10 architecture
findings.summary: The marketing machine is architecturally excellent but operationally hollow; six convergent blockers prevent launch.
findings.impact: The site is not deployable, the security posture prevents customer exposure, analytics are dark, geo routing leaks Arizona visitors, the compliance engine is schema-only, and 99.7% cancelled customers leave the reactivation audience at zero. This finding aggregates the cross-references rather than duplicating them.

findings.title: Zero paid media until Gates 0-3 close
findings.summary: A hard rule: no paid media spend until Gates 0 through 3 are closed.
findings.impact: Not conservative; it prevents wasted spend and compliance exposure. GBP optimization, a draft Ads build, and A2P registration proceed free. Scaling rules: no scaling past 2K/mo until CPL is under 45 dollars for 2 weeks; kill ad groups below 2% CTR after 500 impressions.
